newsitem.title: UK: Mutual funds seen propping high U.S. equity levels.
newsitem.headline: Mutual funds seen propping high U.S. equity levels.

text.p: The U.S. equity market is likely to continue trading above fair value for some time, and U.K. pension funds should look for any sharp correction this year as an opportunity to get back into the market , said Legal and General Investment management.
LGIM investment strategy director David Shaw said on Thursday U.S. equities would maintain a higher than predicted valuation for a number of years, largely as a result of mutual fund flows.
He said the rise in U.S. equities has been driven by a combination of falling issuance, stock retirement and the demographically driven explosion in 401(k) contributions.
Falling issuance and stock retirement were likely to be limited by the corporate sector's gearing ratio, but the 401(k) growth was not expected to peak before 2025, Shaw said.
He said that the hefty rally of the past few years in U.S. equities had resulted in market valuations becoming severely overstretched.
"But markets can and do trade away from fair value if the state of liquidity in the financial system is deficient or excessive."
He said mixed mutual funds had risen to $2,320 billion in 1996 from $605 billion in 1990 and the proportion of their holdings in equities had climbed to 62 percent from 39 percent.

"Analysis of the demand and supply of U.S. equities shows that the total equity market has not grown in recent years and the increased holdings by mutual funds have largely come from the personal sector's direct holdings," he said.
The expected continued demand for 401(k) provision meant that demand for U.S. equities by the mutual fund industry would continue to grow.
He said that UK pension funds, having largely spurned U.S. equities in the last three years amid fears over valuations, should be looking for a way back into the market.
An expected sharp correction in the U.S. market in the short term should offer an opportunity to return to a neutral position.
